segments.expected: "It's for a hand," said Kiva. "That's what's written on it. In two books, under two names. For a hand. Not for a bank, a floor, a crossing or a sale." She made herself go on. "It's Seven's word. It's my captain's name and mine. If it were wanted, I'd have to go to my four and to the Order, and say it was wanted, and ask."

segments.expected: "One mark off eighth. One mark off the roll." He looked at the sheet. "Third last night. Ninth tonight. Fifteenth on the Hunt, with no remarks, with clean work on our stow and a fold called and a pass that held." He was quiet for a moment. "With a dry bag that combed red and a dry bag that combed clean, off the same stow in the same slack, and nobody can say why."
segments.transcript: One mark off eights, one mark off the roll. He looked at the sheet. Third last night, ninth tonight, fifteenth on the hunt, with no remarks, with clean work on our stow, and a fold called and a pass that held. He was quiet for a moment, with a dry bag that combed red and a dry bag that combed clean, off the same stow in the same slack, and nobody can say why.

segments.expected: "It's honest," said Jude again. "I'd want it said that I know it's honest. That nobody gave us anything and nobody took anything." He did not look away from the line. "I don't care about the mark. Tonight. I'll care tomorrow. Tonight I don't."
